title: Stable channel versioning playbook and migration assistant
creator: Asha Patel
description: This ticket defines a single-source playbook for how the Redwood serving runtime moves across stable release channels, how breaking changes and deprecations are classified, and the tooling we will ship (migration assistant + compatibility checker) to make upgrades safe for Dedicated and Private customers. The goal is to reduce upgrade friction, eliminate silent breakages, and enable predictable LTS windows for customers who need long-lived runtime binaries.
tasks: Draft concrete versioning rules (what triggers major/minor/patch) with examples that map to our request surface (REST fields, streaming protocol, model KV format, control-plane flags)
Design 'compatibility-level' server header and client handshake: spec + RFC and wire examples
Implement rwmigrate CLI prototype that runs static checks and a dry-run migration using customer prompt-samples
Add telemetry hooks for preflight upgrade trials: compatibility-check results, sample failure traces, migration cost estimates
Define LTS channel definitions and calendar (Stable, Extended-LTS, Security-only) and retention policy
Create rollout gate definitions (canary %, metric thresholds, manual approval steps) and automate enforcement in CI/CD
Author deprecation header format and automatic 6-month annotation in release notes when API surface is marked deprecated
Integrate compatibility checker into the console: per-route advisories and suggested mitigation (fallback model, rolling restart)
acceptance_criteria: A public doc exists describing exact semver rules for runtime artifacts with 6 concrete examples (e.g., kv cache header change => major, new non-breaking config => minor)
rwmigrate CLI can analyze a running cluster and produce a migration plan report (pass/fail + suggestions) on internal test clusters
Canary rollout automation enforces health gates: error rate increase < 0.1% absolute AND latency P95 within +20% of baseline else rollback
Console shows compatibility warnings for pinned customers and surfaces recommended fallback models when incompatibility detected
Release pipeline emits deprecation headers for deprecated endpoints and auto-generates a 6-month calendar event for follow-up removal
comments: 2026-03-10 - Asha Patel: Kickoff note — scoped initially to runtime network+API contract and kvcache wire format. We'll iterate to cover CLI/tools after initial RFC.

2026-03-11 - Miguel Ramirez: Added initial draft semver mapping. Proposed rule: major for any change that can cause model binary or kv cache incompatibility, minor for additive API features, patch for bugfix/behavioral fixes. Need legal/security signoff for migration data retention notes.

2026-03-12 - Priya Nair (PM): Customer feedback from on-prem pilot: they need a 12-month LTS option for regulated deployments. Proposal: add Extended-LTS paid channel; coordinate with partnerships for SLA language.
2026-03-13 - Eng infra: Early sketch for 'compatibility-level' header: v1, v1-legacy, v2-preview. Need to define handshake semantics for cross-version proxying.
2026-03-14 - Design review: Suggested UI for Console compatibility advisor: red/yellow/green badges per route, with 'migration cost' score and one-click scheduling for a dry-run rollout
notes: Key trade-offs: longer deprecation windows reduce customer churn but increase maintenance burden. Migration assistant will favor non-destructive mitigation (fallback models, runtime flags) before forcing new major releases.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): RFC + semver rule set + compatibility header. Phase 2 (4 weeks): rwmigrate MVP + telemetry + console advisor. Phase 3 (2 weeks): dogfood on internal Dedicated clusters and pilot customers, then announce Stable/LTS calendar. Rollout gating uses canary cohorts (1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) with automated rollback on gate failure.
rollback_strategy: Automatic rollback on gate violation; manual emergency rollback via Console. For major releases impacting protocol, retain a compatibility shim for two LTS windows to allow staggered upgrades.
migration_guidance: Provide per-customer migration report: expected downtime (if any), KV cache migration steps, recommended model pinning strategy, and step-by-step rwmigrate commands. Include sample prompts and unit tests to validate behavior post-upgrade.
risks: Customers with pinned models may encounter N+1 config drift if we change kernel selection behavior — mitigate via pinned kernel hashes in manifest
Silent failures if deprecation headers are ignored by automation — mitigate by surfacing warnings in Console and sending weekly telemetry reports to owners
Operational cost of supporting multiple LTS windows — quantify before approving Extended-LTS sales
